runners_data.name: Fozzie
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse whose true running style places it at the rear, but with several genuine back-markers in this field it is likely to be taken forward into midfield by Shane Gray rather than risk being outpaced from far back; sim-going figures of 4/5 with three places on Good or similar suggest competitiveness without a win.|

runners_data.name: Glen Nevis
runners_data.note: Unknown style with only two runs, both on Good ground where it has placed once; lightly raced flag and Charlie Johnston's strong T14 record (5/45) suggest this runner may be ahead of its mark, and Oliver Stammers will need to find a tactical position early.|

runners_data.name: Indefensible
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner with a solid sim-going record (2 places from 6 on Good) and headgear (hood) suggesting a horse that needs assistance to focus; the closest challenger to Bee Farmer positionally and a logical beneficiary of a controlled pace if it can sustain its effort over 7½f.|

runners_data.name: Wats On Tiger
runners_data.note: Oldest runner in the field at four years and carrying top weight of 142lbs with a going suitability marked UNKNOWN and no recorded last-run date — a significant unknown quantity; Faye McManoman keeps the ride but the absence of any recent form or going data makes this horse very difficult to assess.|

runners_data.name: Bee Farmer
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner, drawn to control this race for Edward Bethell with P J McDonald — arguably the most important horse in the pace map regardless of its raw OR of 120; placed on Good ground over a similar trip and will dictate whether this is a test of stamina or a sprint finish.|

runners_data.name: Elias Escape
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse from the powerful Fahey yard with 31 days since last run and two unplaced efforts on Good ground in its sim-going history; will need a strongly run race to get competitive and the current pace map does not provide that.|

runners_data.name: Lorca's Waltz
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning after a very long 150-day absence with a tongue-tie applied and only Tapeta form in the book — both the layoff and the surface switch to turf on Good ground are significant concerns; William Haggas has not fired a winner from seven runners in the T14 window.|

runners_data.name: Race To The Edge
runners_data.note: Unknown style but has run twice on Good ground over 7f and placed once, giving it relevant experience for today's conditions; Roger Varian's T14 strike rate of 3/24 is respectable and Robbie Downey should be able to find a workable position in a nine-runner field.|

runners_data.name: Melting Snow
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Ed Dunlop who has been active recently (5/19 T14) but the horse itself has been off 35 days; only one sim-going run (unplaced) and a form string of 8-5 suggesting limited progression — needs a strong pace to be involved late.|

races.paceDynamic: Bee Farmer is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with P J McDonald aboard, will look to dictate from the outset over this 7½f Beverley trip on Good ground — expect a controlled, sustainable gallop rather than a scorching pace. Indefensible is the only other horse with genuine prominent form and will likely slot in directly behind Bee Farmer, meaning the leader faces minimal pressure and can control tempo entirely. The hold-up contingent — Fozzie, Elias Escape, Lorca's Waltz, and Melting Snow — will be forced to cover ground from well back, while the unknown-style trio (Glen Nevis, Wats On Tiger, Race To The Edge) add positional uncertainty to the mid-to-rear sections. This shape — a lone, uncontested leader setting a measured pace — strongly favours prominent runners who can stay close to the fractions and pounce in the final two furlongs, while hold-up horses face the dual disadvantage of conceding ground and meeting a pace that may not be strong enough to set up a late finish. The field holds more hold-up types than can all be accommodated at the rear in a meaningful way; Fozzie is the horse most likely displaced from its natural position, redistributed into midfield because the true back markers are numerous and Fozzie's ability to get competitive cover is compromised by this compressed field shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bee Farmer Controls Wire-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Bee Farmer gets a soft lead and Indefensible cannot apply pressure, allowing McDonald to dictate every fraction.
scenarios.body: Bee Farmer settles into a rhythm unchallenged and the hold-up horses never get the strong pace they need to close; the prominent position becomes the winning position as the field strings out chasing a controlled leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Bee Farmer's pace is honest enough to tire slightly in the final furlong, allowing a stalking prominent type to sweep past.
scenarios.body: Indefensible or one of the unknown-style runners who takes a handy position sits just off the pace and finds the extra gears when the leader flattens; the hold-up brigade arrives too late to matter.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Closes Strongly
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than expected and the front end burns out, giving hold-up horses a true target in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Fozzie, with sim-going form to draw on and a trainer in Kevin Ryan who excels at placing horses for this style, would be best placed to exploit a collapsing pace from a midfield berth; Melting Snow or Elias Escape could also make late ground but would need a more extreme collapse.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Unknown Style Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If one of the lightly raced unknown-style runners (Glen Nevis, Wats On Tiger, Race To The Edge) is found to possess unexploited ability and takes a natural prominent position.
scenarios.body: A Roger Varian or Charlie Johnston unknown quantity travelling well in a prominent pitch could be the horse the market hasn't fully priced; Wats On Tiger's higher weight and unknown going preference adds risk, but Race To The Edge's recent 7f Good experience gives it the best credentials of the three.

watchPoints.text: Bee Farmer (P J McDonald) — if he gets a completely uncontested lead from the outset, the race may effectively be over before the turn; watch whether Indefensible or any unknown-style runner pressures him in the first two furlongs.

Wats On Tiger — unknown going suitability, no recorded last-run date, and a 14lbs weight advantage over rivals flipped on its head by top weight of 142lbs; if this horse is unfit or unsuited to Good ground it could cause interference as a potential drifter in running.

Lorca's Waltz — returning from 150 days off with a tongue-tie applied and only artificial-surface form; horses returning from long layoffs at Beverley over 7½f can unsettle pace maps if they go off too eagerly before tiring.

Fozzie — watch whether Shane Gray elects to push forward from the redistributed midfield position or attempts to ride the horse's natural hold-up style; if Gray goes forward, it could complicate Indefensible's prominent pitch and change the race shape mid-race.

runners_data.name: Billyjoegold

runners_data.name: Emerald Army

runners_data.name: Oselton

runners_data.name: Valsharah
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse redistributed to midfield; headgear noted (t) and recent fourth at 7f on Good is the most relevant form — Michael Appleby's runner has placed on Good before and is one of the more interesting closers if gaps open.

runners_data.name: Langholm
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse mapped to midfield; 10-year-old with headgear (tp) and sim-going record of 8/15 including a win on Good — age and recent poor finishes (0-0-8) suggest this is a big ask even if the pace scenario suits.

runners_data.name: Elettaria
runners_data.note: True hold-up type redistributed to midfield; headgear (p) and sim-going record of 8/15 with one place — has run consistently in mid-division at 7-8f on Good but lacks the finishing kick to suggest a win is imminent.

runners_data.name: Hear The Drums
runners_data.note: Hold-up type tagged as fading in the finish — a serious concern; 3-year-old for Fahey carrying just 127lbs but sim-going record of 5/7 with no wins or places on Good and a fade flag make this a difficult proposition.

runners_data.name: Crystal Aurora
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Ivan Furtado; sim-going record of 4/8 and a recent fourth at 8f on Good suggests she stays well — 3-year-old on 127lbs but no win and Robbie Downey must navigate midfield traffic from a disadvantaged position.

runners_data.name: Lope Y Linda
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Tim Easterby, one of the highest-strike-rate trainers in this field (T14: 6/89); recent win at 7f on Good and sim-going record of 7/10 are strong credentials — Jake Dickson (7) is a claim booking, the only minor doubt in what is an otherwise compelling prominent-horse profile.

races.paceDynamic: Emerald Army is the sole confirmed front-runner and will lead from the outset at Beverley's 7½f trip, setting a sustainable, uncontested pace on Good ground with James Sullivan able to dictate entirely on his own terms. Lope Y Linda and I Can Boogy will push forward to press for prominent positions just off the leader, but with no genuine pace rival to Emerald Army, the gallop is unlikely to be truly searching. This field is packed with hold-up types — Bantz, Billyjoegold, Summer Rain, Indy's Angel, Valsharah, Langholm, and Elettaria are all natural hold-up horses redistributed into midfield on the map because there are far more closers than the rear of the race can physically accommodate; the horses most likely to actually secure prominent ground are Lope Y Linda and I Can Boogy given their natural style, while the genuine hold-up runners must accept traffic and a bunched finish. With a steady to moderate pace set by one uncontested leader, this race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently in second or third, as the lack of true pressure means the front end will rarely be softened up sufficiently for pure closers to cut through.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Emerald Army Leads Untroubled
scenarios.trigger: If Emerald Army is allowed to dictate a moderate pace and kicks clear from 2f out without being seriously pressed.
scenarios.body: Emerald Army's recent form of consecutive placed efforts at 7f on Good ground, combined with an uncontested lead, gives him every chance of converting; Ruth Carr's runner has shown a strong tendency to be placed when in front and James Sullivan will exploit the situation to the full.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Lope Y Linda and I Can Boogy push hard to track Emerald Army and the race develops into a battle between the front three.
scenarios.body: Lope Y Linda's recent win at 7f on Good for Easterby's yard and her progressive profile makes her a prime beneficiary if the pace is honest enough to test Emerald Army; I Can Boogy's sim-going record of 9/15 and placed efforts at similar trips add further credibility to a prominent-horse finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If Lope Y Linda or I Can Boogy push the pace hard enough to string the field out and create genuine gaps for closers.
scenarios.body: Valsharah has a recent fourth at 7f on Good and Oselton has shown tactical flexibility with wins at 7f on Standard, and if the pace finally has some zip the well-held runners can deliver; Miss Willows, a course-distance winner last time on Soft, is the outsider of this group who could benefit from any late surge of stamina.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Handicap Produces Messy Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the large hold-up cluster causes interference and traffic trouble in the straight, producing a chaotic blanket finish.
scenarios.body: With so many horses forced into a compressed midfield group and jockeys fighting for runs, Elettaria and Langholm — both placed horses on Good ground with course experience — could sneak through gaps in a scrappy finish; this is the least likely scenario but the sheer number of closers makes chaos a non-trivial possibility.

watchPoints.text: Emerald Army is the sole uncontested front-runner — if James Sullivan is allowed to stride clear at his own pace, the rest of the field may never get close enough to challenge on this Good ground.

Lope Y Linda represents the most likely challenger to Emerald Army from a prominent position; if Jake Dickson (7lb claimer) pushes forward assertively, a straight duel between these two is the most probable finish shape.

The large cluster of hold-up horses — Bantz, Billyjoegold, Summer Rain, Indy's Angel, Valsharah, Langholm, and Elettaria — all need to find gaps in a compressed midfield group; watch for traffic trouble and interference in the straight as multiple jockeys look for room simultaneously.

Hear The Drums and Billyjoegold are both tagged as fading in the finish — if either is placed prominently by their jockeys against their natural style in an attempt to overcome this, they could cause interference when tiring inside the final furlong.

Miss Willows recorded a course-distance win last time but that came on Soft ground — the step back to Good removes that edge and her sim-going record of 10/15 suggests the surface shift is worth monitoring in running.

runners_data.name: Dream Deal
runners_data.note: Another genuine hold-up type redistributed to midfield on the map; all recent form is at 6f on good or standard, making this 5f trip a potential concern — Tim Easterby yard is in strong form (9/102) but the distance is shorter than preferred.|

runners_data.name: Bibendum
runners_data.note: Prominent type who maps to sit close to Keldeo; visor worn, recent form moderate, and all five recent runs have been on standard or soft ground — the good surface here is a mild positive flag but 5f form is limited.|

races.paceDynamic: Keldeo is the sole confirmed front-runner and will set off to lead from stall, likely dictating at a sustainable, uncontested gallop over this flat 5f on good turf — no other confirmed leader will push him for the front. Azuinthejungle and Bibendum are the prominent types most likely to track him closely in second and third, while Miss Brazen, Fierce, Spirit Of Applause, Jojo Rabbit, Ay Gee Ell, Lord Abama and Dream Deal will all need to come from behind to varying degrees. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the map can place at the rear — Ay Gee Ell, Jojo Rabbit, Lord Abama and Dream Deal are genuine closers redistributed to midfield on the map but will in reality be running on from the back half of the field. With one uncontested leader setting a controlled, honest but not punishing tempo, this race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with proven finishing kick on good ground, as the pace is unlikely to be fast enough to string the field out and those coming late will have room to challenge in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Keldeo Leads Unapposed, Closers Fly
scenarios.trigger: If Keldeo bowls along at a comfortable solo lead and hold-up horses get clear runs in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Keldeo's uncontested lead on good ground sets a steady tempo that compresses the field, allowing well-handicapped closers to reel him in late; Miss Brazen and Fierce, both proven 5f good-ground performers with strong recent form, are ideally suited to finishing strongly into a slow-run contest.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Pair Clear, Rail Battle
scenarios.trigger: If Azuinthejungle or Bibendum push up alongside Keldeo early and the front trio break clear.
scenarios.body: A modestly faster pace develops with two or three horses prominent throughout, favouring those who can travel comfortably in the first half of the race and sustain it; Keldeo, who has tactical speed and won recently on good, and Azuinthejungle, who maps to track the leader, are positioned to benefit if closers get blocked or outpaced.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Traffic, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up horses get bunched in a pack and one manages to find a clear lane late.
scenarios.body: With so many genuine closers in the field, traffic and interference in the closing stages is a real risk, but one clean-running finisher from the back half could land the prize; Jojo Rabbit, who has placed multiple times on similar ground and is handled by the experienced James Sullivan, and Ay Gee Ell, who has shown consistent placed form at this trip, are dangers if they thread through.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely dawdling and the closers simply cannot make up ground in time on this flat 5f.
scenarios.body: A truly unhurried tempo allows front-runners and prominent types to conserve energy and sprint clear inside the final furlong, with hold-up horses stranded too far back to peg them back in time; Keldeo, fresh from a recent win and comfortable on good ground, and Bibendum, mapping prominently with Cam Hardie, are the primary beneficiaries.

watchPoints.text: Keldeo's uncontested lead means if he quickens two furlongs out before closers have balanced, he could simply not be caught — watch whether Azuinthejungle or Bibendum push the pace early enough to force a genuine test.|
Spirit Of Applause has not run for 211 days and all recent form is on standard ground — if bursting with freshness she could unsettle the pace shape, but fitness on return is a real question.|

With Ay Gee Ell, Jojo Rabbit, Lord Abama and Dream Deal all genuine hold-up horses forced wide or into traffic in the closing stages, a pile-up of closers fighting for the same gap on the far rail is a real risk inside the final furlong.|
Lord Abama and Dream Deal have both been running at 6f recently — if the shorter 5f trip catches them out for pace early, they may not get competitive positions even from the rear of the field.|
Bibendum wears a visor and is trained by Julie Camacho whose yard is 4/22 over the past 14 days — worth monitoring in-race for any eyecatching move from a prominent position if the pace drops off.|

runners_data.name: Rogers Dream

races.paceDynamic: This 1m½f Beverley handicap is an all-hold-up affair with every single runner in the field carrying a genuine rear-to-midfield style — there is no confirmed front-runner and no horse likely to willingly set a strong gallop from the outset. The result will almost certainly be a dawdling, bunched procession through the early stages before a sharp, compressed sprint develops in the straight, favouring those with late finishing speed over those who need a genuine test of stamina. The field holds far more hold-up types than the race map can physically place at the rear; Copper And Five, Can I Kiss You, Little Ted, Rogers Dream, Mavetheforcebewivu, and Anificas Beauty are all genuine closers who will be competing for the same back-division real estate, meaning several will inevitably be pushed forward into a false midfield position against their nature. With no pace injection anticipated, the tactical verdict is clear: horses with sharp sprint-finish ability over this trip in good ground — and those handily enough placed when the sprint ignites — are most favoured, while deep stayers reliant on a true gallop to bring their stamina into play are at a significant disadvantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish Carnage
scenarios.trigger: If the field crawls early and bunches into a fierce two-furlong dash home
scenarios.body: With no gallop to string the field out, the final two furlongs will be a chaotic scramble for position and those with the sharpest finishing acceleration on good ground will dominate; horses proven in similar sprint-finish scenarios at this trip benefit enormously.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: False Position Favours Handy
scenarios.trigger: If a horse drifts to the front by default and sets a modest but honest pace
scenarios.body: A runner stumbling into the lead — most likely Hostelry or Wicklow Way by accident rather than design — creates a slightly more strung-out race that rewards those able to track closer than their natural style dictates; midfield-from-wide positions become golden.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Stamina Prevails Uphill
scenarios.trigger: If rain or a firmer-than-expected strip adds genuine stamina emphasis to the climb
scenarios.body: The Beverley straight has a stiff uphill finish that can expose sprint-only types if even a modest true pace is set; horses with proven form at 10f-12f distances and good-ground stamina come into play.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Trouble In Running
scenarios.trigger: If a badly positioned or boxed-in hold-up horse loses ground at a critical stage in the sprint
scenarios.body: With eight genuine hold-up horses all competing for the same late runs, traffic problems are a near certainty for at least one runner; the horse that finds a clean passage soonest gains a decisive advantage regardless of overall form.

watchPoints.text: Copper And Five and Little Ted will be fighting for identical late-run positions in a condensed sprint — if either gets squeezed or checked entering the straight, their chance evaporates instantly.

With eight hold-up horses and no genuine pace, the opening half-mile could be dangerously slow, making the final two-furlong sprint so compressed that draw and early positioning in the home straight become race-defining factors.

Hostelry's jockey Tom Kiely-Marshall(5) is a claiming apprentice on a hold-up horse in a race with no pace — navigating traffic in a bunched sprint finish will require significant experience that the 5lb claimer may not yet possess.

Anificas Beauty's proportionally strong good-ground record (2W2P from 5 runs) could be misleading given the step up from recent 6f-7f runs — monitor in the market to see if connections believe the trip extension suits.

Rogers Dream carries a disqualification (D) in recent form — connections and punters should note any veterinary or stewards' history that could affect how the horse travels in a tightly packed, slow-run field.

runners_data.name: Pureis King
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up runner who fades in the finish — a significant concern given this race is unlikely to have a strong enough pace to set up a late burst; only 3 runs in the book, sim-going record 1W1P from just 6 runs; the finish fade flag makes this 1m2f trip on a stiff course a risk.|

races.paceDynamic: Inspiring Speeches is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m2f trip on good ground at Beverley. Hijo De La Luna is the one prominent type likely to push up alongside or just behind, but with Inspiring Speeches uncontested, the pace is unlikely to be truly searching. This field contains more hold-up and prominent types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Pureis King, Dandy's Angel, Sweet Cicely, Regal Glory and Rajawail are all natural hold-up horses who will be competing for the same ground in midfield and behind, meaning the race shape is likely to be strung out with a cluster chasing through the home straight. A controlled, front-running tempo on good ground at Beverley — where the straight rises stiffly — tends to reward horses with proven stamina and a prominent position from which they can sustain their effort; purely hold-up horses who need a strong gallop to get competitive are at a disadvantage here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Inspiring Speeches Leads, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Inspiring Speeches is allowed a soft lead and the pace remains steady throughout, allowing her stamina advantage to kick in up the Beverley straight.
scenarios.body: Inspiring Speeches bowls along uncontested, sets a modest tempo and uses her confirmed front-running style to control the race; the strong Beverley finish tests the hold-up horses who struggle to close from the rear on a comfortable gallop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is moderate enough to compress the field and a hold-up runner produced with a well-timed run gets first run at the top of the straight.
scenarios.body: With the field bunched behind a solo leader, a horse like Quirke On Parole or Daring Leader travelling sweetly in midfield can burst through late; Beverley's stiff finish doesn't entirely negate a late run if the fractions are slow early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Picks Up
scenarios.trigger: If Hijo De La Luna or a horse who secures a prominent position travels comfortably and pounces before the true hold-up types get organised.
scenarios.body: A horse travelling just off Inspiring Speeches in second or third is perfectly placed to capitalise at Beverley where grinding out a position in the straight matters more than a late burst; Hijo De La Luna has course-relevant form and acts on good ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If Inspiring Speeches sets an unusually slow pace and the whole field arrives together turning for home, turning the race into a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: In a truly muddling race, raw form differences compress and a horse like Pureis King or Rajawail carrying lower weight could fluke into frame contention; however the Beverley straight punishes non-stayers and horses with stamina doubts.

watchPoints.text: Inspiring Speeches is uncontested up front — watch whether Tom Kiely-Marshall (5lb claimer) sends her clear early or allows an overly slow gallop, as either extreme will have major consequences for the finish.
Hijo De La Luna wears a visor and has a history of idling when in front — watch the opening two furlongs to see if he takes up a prominent position or is settled further back than expected.

Quirke On Parole and Daring Leader are both hold-up runners relying on a genuine gallop; if the pace is soft, watch whether they get shuffled into an impossible position as the midfield becomes crowded with similarly-styled horses.

Sweet Cicely is fitted with blinkers and has run poorly in recent starts — watch for whether a headgear-aided improvement is signalled in the market before the off, as a move in price would indicate stable confidence in a revival.

Pureis King is tagged as a horse that fades in the finish; watch for any early position change — if the horse moves forward conspicuously early, it may suggest the jockey is trying to compensate for the stamina concern over 1m2f.
